quote: The Szilassi polyhedron is named after Hungarian mathematician Lajos Szilassi, who discovered it in 1977.
note: The problem asks whether a non-convex, non-self-intersecting polyhedron with more than seven faces exists where every pair of faces shares an edge. The Szilassi polyhedron (7 faces) was discovered in 1977, establishing the upper bound known at that time. The problem of whether such a polyhedron exists with more than 7 faces remained open.
